newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics cites shipment shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics cites shipment shortfall.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc Chairman and CEO Edward McCracken said he was disappointed with the company's inability to reach expected shipment levels due to delays in gearing up manufacturing of new products.

"Despite our strong bookings, we did not reach expected levels of shipments, due to delays in manufacturing ramp-up for some of our new products announced on October 7 and variations in product mix," he said in a statement. The company said its consolidated backlog was $757 million at December 31, 1996 and product bookings hit $955 million -- both of which were the highest levels ever for the company.
"While I'm disappointed in the results, I am encouraged by our customers' enthusiastic response to our new product line, as evidenced by our strong bookings and backlog," he said.
"We also had continued strong demand for Cray Research supercomputers," the chairman and chief executive said.

The company said its market position was "substantially improved" as a result of the new desktop and high-end product families it introduced in October, along with a new architecture which it described as "revolutionary."
The new architecture runs throughout SGI's products, from its desktop and deskside Web servers and computers that can hold organization-wide databases to its supercomputers.

The shortfall had been pre-announced by Silicon Graphics on January 6. The company's second quarter revenues of $825 million and net earnings per share of $0.01, prior to merger charges of $14 million related to its aquisition of Cray Research, were consistent with its pre-announcement warning.
The company has been struggling to carry out its largest product transition in years, and a string of consecutive earnings disappointments which date back more than a year.
